Processing Steps: 1. Install OpenCV, NumPy, Matplotlib | 2. Set up folder structure: /input /output /src /tests | 3. Create config.py for constants (grid size, colors, thresholds)
Output: requirements.txt with pinned versions | Folder scaffold ready | config.py with all magic numbers centralized
Specification: Python 3.10+, OpenCV 4.x, NumPy, Matplotlib. No hardcoded values outside config.py.

Processing Steps: 1. Capture 15–20 screenshots covering varied board states | 2. Include edge cases: empty board, nearly full board, each of the 7 pieces as active
Output: Labeled dataset in /input/screenshots/ | Notes file describing each screenshot's board state for ground truth
Specification: PNG format, consistent resolution. At least one screenshot per tetromino type. At least 3 showing the next-piece preview box.

Processing Steps: 1. Resize to standard resolution | 2. Convert to grayscale | 3. Apply Gaussian blur to reduce noise | 4. Apply binary thresholding (Otsu's method)
Output: Preprocessed binary image (numpy array) | Intermediate debug images saved to /output/debug/
Specification: Function: preprocess(img) → binary_img. Must handle both light and dark Tetris themes. Threshold values tunable via config.py.

Processing Steps: 1. Find contours using cv2.findContours | 2. Filter by aspect ratio (~0.5 for a 20x10 grid) | 3. Apply perspective correction if needed using homography | 4. Crop and isolate the board region
Output: Cropped board image (numpy array) | Board bounding box coordinates | Perspective transform matrix (saved for later use)
Specification: Function: detect_board(binary_img) → (board_img, bbox, transform_matrix). Must work even if board is not perfectly axis-aligned.

Processing Steps: 1. Divide board into 20x10 grid of cells | 2. For each cell compute mean pixel intensity | 3. Threshold intensity to classify cell as filled (1) or empty (0) | 4. Build binary 20x10 matrix
Output: 20x10 numpy array of 0s and 1s representing board state | Debug image with grid overlay drawn
Specification: Function: parse_grid(board_img) → np.ndarray shape (20,10). Accuracy target: >95% correct cells on test screenshots.

Processing Steps: 1. Isolate the active piece region (top of board) | 2. Apply blob analysis / connected component labeling | 3. Extract shape mask | 4. Compute Hu moments to classify piece type (I O T S Z J L)
Output: Piece type as string e.g. 'T' | Piece shape as 4x4 binary matrix | Piece position (row, col) on board
Specification: Function: detect_piece(screenshot, bbox) → (piece_type, shape_matrix, position). Must distinguish all 7 tetromino types. Fallback: color-based classification if moments fail.

Processing Steps: 1. Locate the next-piece preview box using template matching or fixed ROI from config | 2. Crop preview region | 3. Apply same blob + Hu moments classification as active piece
Output: Next piece type as string | Next piece shape matrix
Specification: Function: detect_next_piece(screenshot) → (piece_type, shape_matrix). Preview box coordinates stored in config.py since they are fixed per game version.

Processing Steps: 1. Generate all 4 rotations using np.rot90 | 2. Deduplicate (O-piece has 1 unique rotation, I-piece has 2 etc.) | 3. For each rotation compute valid drop columns (where piece fits within board width)
Output: List of unique rotation matrices | For each rotation: list of valid drop columns
Specification: Function: get_rotations(shape_matrix) → list of (rotation_matrix, valid_columns). Must handle all 7 piece types correctly.

Input: Board state matrix (20x10), piece rotation matrix, drop column
Processing Steps: 1. Simulate piece falling — find lowest row it can occupy | 2. Place piece on board copy | 3. Detect and clear completed lines | 4. Return resulting board state
Output: New board state matrix after placement | Number of lines cleared by this move
Specification: Function: simulate_drop(board, piece, col) → (new_board, lines_cleared). Must not mutate original board. Must handle piece going out of bounds gracefully.

Input: Board state matrix (20x10), piece just placed, lines cleared
Processing Steps: 1. Compute all 6 Dellacherie features: landing height, eroded cells, row transitions, column transitions, holes, cumulative wells | 2. Apply weights: -landing_height + eroded_cells - row_transitions - column_transitions - 4*holes - cumulative_wells
Output: Score (float) for this board state | Dictionary of individual feature values for debugging
Specification: Function: dellacherie_score(board, piece, lines_cleared) → (score, features_dict). Weights: holes×(-4), wells×(-1), row_trans×(-1), col_trans×(-1), landing×(-1), eroded×(+1).

Input: Board state, active piece, next piece
Processing Steps: 1. For each rotation of active piece × each valid column → simulate drop → get board state 1 | 2. For each board state 1: for each rotation of next piece × each valid column → simulate drop → score with Dellacherie | 3. Best score for active piece move = max score across all next-piece follow-ups | 4. Select active piece move that maximizes this best-case score
Output: Best (rotation, column) for active piece | Score for each (rotation, column) combination as a 2D array
Specification: Function: best_move(board, active_piece, next_piece) → (best_rotation, best_col, scores_matrix). Scores matrix shape: (num_rotations × 10). Performance target: <500ms per call.

Input: Original screenshot, best rotation, best column, board bounding box
Processing Steps: 1. Draw piece ghost at recommended drop column using cv2 drawing functions | 2. Highlight the target column with a colored rectangle | 3. Annotate with text: recommended rotation and score
Output: Annotated screenshot image saved to /output/ | Display via cv2.imshow or matplotlib
Specification: Function: annotate_move(screenshot, best_rotation, best_col, bbox) → annotated_img. Color: green for best move, white text. Must not obscure board content.

Input: Original screenshot, scores matrix (num_rotations x 10), board bounding box
Processing Steps: 1. Flatten scores to per-column max score (best rotation per column) | 2. Normalize scores to 0–1 range | 3. Map scores to color using cv2 colormap (COLORMAP_RdYlGn) | 4. Overlay semi-transparent colored bars on each column
Output: Heatmap-annotated screenshot saved to /output/heatmap/ | Color legend drawn on image (low = red, high = green)
Specification: Function: draw_heatmap(screenshot, scores_matrix, bbox) → heatmap_img. Transparency alpha=0.4. Legend must always be visible in corner.

Processing Steps: 1. Chain all modules: preprocess → detect_board → parse_grid → detect_piece → detect_next_piece → best_move → annotate + heatmap | 2. Log each step with timing info | 3. Save all outputs to /output/
Output: Annotated screenshot | Heatmap screenshot | Console output: detected pieces, board state, best move, scores | Timing report per step
Specification: Entry point: main.py --input path/to/screenshot.png. Must complete full pipeline in <2 seconds on a standard laptop.

Input: 20 labeled test screenshots with known ground truth
Processing Steps: 1. Run pipeline on all test screenshots | 2. Compare detected board state vs ground truth | 3. Compare recommended move vs manually verified best move | 4. Report accuracy metrics
Output: Accuracy report: grid parsing %, piece detection %, move correctness % | Failure cases documented with debug images
Specification: Target: >90% grid parsing accuracy, >85% piece detection accuracy. All failures must produce a graceful error message, not a crash.

Input: Screen recording of a Tetris game (.mp4)
Processing Steps: 1. Extract frames using cv2.VideoCapture | 2. Detect frame changes using frame differencing to trigger pipeline only on new piece spawns | 3. Run full pipeline on each trigger frame | 4. Write annotated frames to output video
Output: Annotated output video saved to /output/video/ | FPS and processing time report
Specification: Function: process_video(video_path). Trigger threshold: mean frame difference > threshold (tunable in config.py). Output video at same FPS as input.
